title: Readiness Gap Analysis — Why Non-Certifiable Inventory Reaches Certification Boards
readiness_failure_rate_detail: At S809 certification board, 38/38 Domain E seeds were assessed. Gate 1 (Technical Accuracy) passed 38/38. Gate 2 (Explanation Quality) FAILED 38/38 — 53 empty DL-026 slots, 8 DL-013 boilerplate slots, 12 weak ECs. Board verdict: CERTIFY 0, HOLD 38, ESCALATE 0. Zero items certifiable on arrival.

top_readiness_gaps.gap: No pre-board structural defect scan exists
top_readiness_gaps.root_cause: Items in 'Unprocessed' state arrive at certification boards without any empirical structural scan for known defect classes. The S808 seed inventory explicitly noted: 'Requires structural defect scan (DL-008, DL-013, DL-026) before certification' — yet the scan was deferred to the certification board itself. The board was forced to discover defects that should have been caught by a pre-board gate.
top_readiness_gaps.proposed_prevention: Mandatory pre-board structural scan gate. Before any item enters certification board review, run automated scans for: (a) DL-026 empty non-CC EW slots, (b) DL-013 boilerplate patterns, (c) DL-008 non-empty EW[CC], (d) COSO/ASC citation presence, (e) EC minimum-length check. Items failing any structural check must return to remediation queue before board assessment.
top_readiness_gaps.evidence: S808_SEED_INVENTORY.json §38 block: 'structural_defects: DL-008, DL-013, DL-026 must be scanned and remediated before six-dimension verification can proceed.' S809 found 53 empty slots + 8 boilerplate at the board — these were known-risk defect classes that were never scanned pre-board.

top_readiness_gaps.gap: DL-016 metadata-content CC shift corrupts readiness scoring
top_readiness_gaps.root_cause: Packs C and D use dual-block architecture where ChoiceA-D in the metadata block can differ from Choices.A-D in the content block (DL-016). Different agents reading different blocks extract different CorrectChoice values. S320 readiness scoring reports CC values that are systematically wrong for most items — e.g., P1-EC-004 scored with CC='A' (from metadata block) when content-block CC='D'. The readiness board literally cannot determine if an item is ready because it's reading the wrong correct answer.
top_readiness_gaps.proposed_prevention: Standardize CC extraction: boundary-aware same-object Function constructor parse must be the sole authoritative CC source. Any readiness scoring board must use this methodology. Cross-check: if metadata-block ChoiceA-D differs from content-block Choices.A-D by more than trivial whitespace, flag as DL-016 and quarantine from certification until resolved.
top_readiness_gaps.evidence: S320_READINESS_SCORING.json vs SESSION809_SEED_INVENTORY.json: P1-EC-004 CC=A (S320) vs CC=D (inventory), P1-EC-008 CC=A vs D, P1-EC-014 CC=C vs B, P1-EC-021 CC=B vs A, P1-EC-022 CC=C vs B, P1-EC-023 CC=D vs C, P1-EC-024 CC=A vs D — 100% mismatch rate for first 8 Pack C items. S810.1 Agent B found 5 cross-agent CC discrepancies (EC-008, EC-014, EC-031, EC-066, EC-072) all caused by DL-016 shift.

top_readiness_gaps.gap: Certification board serves as defect-discovery vehicle instead of certification gate
top_readiness_gaps.items_affected: All 38 Domain E seeds + broader pattern across all Unprocessed sections
top_readiness_gaps.root_cause: The S809 certification board deployed 28 agents (A-Z + AA) to perform what should have been pre-board work: duplicate prevention audit, EW integrity scan, COSO citation mapping, difficulty calibration, cognitive level alignment, metadata completeness check. All 38 items arrived at the board with ZERO pre-board screening. The board was forced to be a defect-discovery session, not a certification session. S810 (remediation) and S810.1 (intelligence gathering) then had to be spawned as follow-up sessions to address the defects discovered at the board. The pipeline is: bring to board → discover defects → spawn remediation session → bring back to board. Correct pipeline should be: pre-board scan → remediate → bring to board.
top_readiness_gaps.proposed_prevention: Split certification board into two phases. Phase 0 (automated): run all structural scans, DL-026/DL-013/DL-008 detection, CC verification, COSO citation check, metadata completeness. Only items passing Phase 0 advance to Phase 1 (human/agent certification board). Phase 0 exits must produce a signed readiness certificate with per-defect-class status. Items failing any structural check return to remediation without consuming board agent resources.
top_readiness_gaps.evidence: S809 deployed 28 agents. S809.1 deployed 8 more. S810.1 deployed 11 agents. S810 deployed 7 workstreams across 3 agents + 1 patch. Total: ~49 agent deployments across 4 sessions to process 38 items — because defects were discovered at the board rather than before it.

top_readiness_gaps.gap: Unprocessed items are brought to boards with known documentation of their unknown state
top_readiness_gaps.items_affected: ~187 Unprocessed items pool-wide (132 Archived + 187 Unprocessed per S802)
top_readiness_gaps.root_cause: The 'Unprocessed' state is documented as 'Not yet audited' (QUESTION_METADATA_STANDARD.md §1.7.1). The S808 seed inventory explicitly stated: 'Status: Not yet in audit pipeline. Requires structural defect scan (DL-008, DL-013, DL-026) before certification. Estimated per seed: structural scan = 3 minutes, six-dimension verification = 5 minutes = 8 minutes total.' Yet the items were advanced from Unprocessed directly to the S809 certification board with zero intermediate structural screening. The state machine (Unprocessed → In Audit → Certified) was bypassed: items went Unprocessed → Certification Board without ever entering 'In Audit.'
top_readiness_gaps.proposed_prevention: Enforce state machine: Unprocessed items MUST transition to 'In Audit' before reaching any certification board. The 'In Audit' transition must be gated by automated structural scan producing a signed pass report. No item may skip 'In Audit' and proceed directly from 'Unprocessed' to certification board. This state machine enforcement should be automated in governance-guard (proposed Rule 6).
top_readiness_gaps.evidence: S809_SEED_INVENTORY.json: all 38 items show question_state: 'Unprocessed'. S809 certification board assessed them directly — no intermediate 'In Audit' pipeline. S808_SEED_INVENTORY.json §38: 'question_state: Unprocessed. Not yet in audit pipeline.' — explicit acknowledgement that items hadn't entered 'In Audit' before the S809 board.

top_readiness_gaps.gap: Cross-session CC drift makes readiness measurement unreliable
top_readiness_gaps.items_affected: At least 38 seeds, potentially all dual-block Pack C/D items
top_readiness_gaps.root_cause: Multiple sessions/agents independently extract CorrectChoice using different methodologies (regex forward-scan, backward-scan, Function constructor parse, metadata-block lookup, content-block lookup). When DL-016 causes those methodologies to hit different blocks, every session reports different CC values. S809 seed inventory, S320 readiness scoring, S809.1 EW audit, and S810.1 agent outputs all contain conflicting CC values for the same items. The readiness board's HOLD/READY classification is based on CC-dependent metrics (DL-008, DL-026) — with wrong CC, the classification is meaningless.
top_readiness_gaps.proposed_prevention: Define CC as a Certified Pool Attribute (CPA) with a single canonical extraction methodology defined at the governance level and enforced by the governance guard. All agents, boards, and scans must reference the CPA rather than independently extracting CC. The CPA for each QID is published once (by boundary-aware same-object Function constructor parse from the authoritative source file) and all downstream processes consume it as a trusted reference. Any agent that independently re-derives CC must cross-check against the CPA publication and flag discrepancies.
top_readiness_gaps.evidence: Cross-session CC table: P1-EC-004: S809_inventory='D', S320_board='A', S810.1_AgentC='D'. P1-EC-008: S809='D', S320='A', S810.1_AgentC_metadata='D', S810.1_AgentD_content='A'. P1-EC-014: S809='B', S320='C', S810.1_AgentC='C', S810.1_AgentD='B'. P1-EC-020: S809='D', S320='A'. P1-EC-021: S809='A', S320='B'. — At least 18 of 38 seeds have conflicting CC across sessions, making readiness board scoring unreliable for those items.

top_readiness_gaps.gap: Readiness board exists but cannot block certification board scheduling
top_readiness_gaps.root_cause: The S318 Readiness Board correctly identified prerequisites (C1: Wave 2b recovery needed; seed certification pipeline authorization needed). It authorized S319 with clear constraints. But the readiness board has no enforcement mechanism — it's an advisory document. S319 → S808 → S809 → S810 all proceeded, and the seeds reached the S809 certification board regardless of whether pre-board conditions from S318 were actually satisfied. The readiness board says 'READY FOR S319 with conditions' but cannot prevent S809 from happening if conditions aren't met.
top_readiness_gaps.proposed_prevention: Give the readiness board enforcement power. A readiness board VERDICT must be machine-readable (JSON boolean 'blocked': true/false). The governance guard or session startup protocol should check the most recent readiness board verdict before allowing any certification board to convene. If `blocked: true` or conditions_outstanding > 0, the certification board session must abort with a reference to the unsatisfied readiness condition. The board must be explicitly cleared (conditions → resolved) by a subsequent readiness refresh before certification can proceed.
top_readiness_gaps.evidence: S318_READINESS_BOARD.json: verdict='READY FOR S319', conditions_outstanding=0, conditions_reframed_as_work_items=2 (registry rebuild, seed dedup audit). S319 focused on seed pipeline authorization. S809 then convened a full certification board over the same seeds without an intermediate readiness check. The chain S318→S319→S808→S809 shows no readiness board between S808 (clone insertion) and S809 (certification board).

readiness_board_effectiveness.evidence: S318 Readiness Board correctly identified prerequisites and authorized S319 with conditions. It resolved C1 (Wave 2b blocker). However, the board has no enforcement mechanism — items bypass the readiness pipeline. The S808 seed inventory explicitly warned 'Requires structural defect scan before certification' but the S809 certification board assessed the items anyway. The S320 readiness scoring was corrupted by DL-016 CC mismatch (18+ of 38 items had wrong CC values), producing erroneous HOLD/READY classifications. The 4 items scored READY by S320 (ED-028, ED-042, ED-046, ED-051) were based on CC values that don't match the source files — making the READY verdict unreliable. Additionally, no readiness board convened between S808's clone insertion and S809's certification board, meaning items went from clone archival directly to certification assessment with zero interim readiness gate. The board is an advisory document, not an enforcement mechanism.
gaps_identified: No machine-readable blocked/cleared flag to prevent certification board from convening
No automated check that readiness conditions were satisfied before certification board session
Readiness scoring methodology (CC extraction) not standardized — S320 used different CC values than S809
No pre-board structural defect scan integrated into readiness gate
Readiness board doesn't track which prerequisite scans were actually executed vs. deferred

pre_board_scan_gaps: DL-026 empty non-CC EW slot scan: NOT RUN before S809 board. Board discovered 53 empty slots across 38 seeds.
DL-013 boilerplate scan: NOT RUN before S809 board. Board discovered 8 boilerplate slots across 5 Pack D seeds.

DL-008 non-empty EW[CC] scan: RUN but methodology unreliable. S809 found 0 DL-008. However CC values used for this scan were from metadata block, not authoritative content block — DL-016 CC shift. If CC values were wrong, the DL-008 scan could be systemically missing violations.
COSO/ASC citation presence check: NOT RUN. Board discovered only 1 of 38 seeds (2.6%) had a COSO citation. 37 of 38 had zero citations.
EC minimum-length / quality check: NOT RUN. Board discovered 12 seeds with weak ECs (below CAQS §4 mini-lesson standard).
Difficulty ↔ DifficultyScore consistency: NOT RUN. Board discovered 14 label/score mismatches and 23 of 38 (60.5%) difficulty overstated.
CognitiveLevel alignment: NOT RUN. Board discovered 26 of 38 (68.4%) CL misaligned.
AccountingPrinciple field presence: NOT RUN. Board discovered 38 of 38 (100%) missing this field.
CorrectChoice cross-verification (content-block vs. metadata-block): NOT RUN before S809. S810.1 discovered 5 seeds with CC discrepancies between agents — blocker for any remediation.

DL-016 metadata-content mismatch scan: NOT RUN. All 38 seeds affected — metadata ChoiceA-D describes +1 neighbor's topic, not current item's topic. This corrupts any ExplanationWrong quality assessment.
Blueprint LOS-to-topic mapping: NOT RUN. Board discovered 0 seeds had explicit LOS-topic mappings.

specific_defects_missed_by_pre_board_rea.DL-026 empty EW slots: 53 slots across 38 seeds (100% affected). These are structurally detectable (field-presence + empty-string check). Missed because no pre-board scan was configured.
specific_defects_missed_by_pre_board_rea.DL-013 boilerplate: 8 slots across 5 seeds. Pattern: 'does not align with COSO... represents a plausible misconception'. Regex-detectable. Missed because no pre-board scan.
specific_defects_missed_by_pre_board_rea.DL-016 metadata-content shift: 38/38 seeds (100%). Metadata ChoiceA-D describes +1 neighbor's topic. This is the root cause defect explaining why readiness boards and scans produce conflicting CC values. NOT scannable by simple regex — requires same-object CC verification.
specific_defects_missed_by_pre_board_rea.Missing COSO citations: 37/38 seeds (97%). Only P1-EC-008 had a COSO reference. Field-scan detectable (grep for 'COSO' in EC field). Missed.
specific_defects_missed_by_pre_board_rea.Weak ECs: 12 seeds (31.6%) below CAQS §4 mini-lesson standard. Length-based threshold combined with keyword presence check (standard name, formula, business context). Missed.
specific_defects_missed_by_pre_board_rea.Difficulty inflation (DL-031): 12 seeds (31.6%) are definition-match items labeled Moderate instead of Easy. Semantic detection needed — stem-definition → answer-term pattern.
specific_defects_missed_by_pre_board_rea.CognitiveLevel misalignment: 26/38 (68.4%). 12 labeled Understand that test Remember (definition recall). 7 labeled Apply that test Understand (conceptual explanation). Semantic detection needed.

systematic_pattern_detail: YES. There is a documented systematic pattern where Unprocessed items with known defect classes (DL-026, DL-013, DL-008 risk, DL-016) are brought to certification boards. Evidence: (1) S808 seed inventory explicitly warned 'Requires structural defect scan (DL-008, DL-013, DL-026) before certification.' (2) Despite this warning, no structural scan was run before S809. (3) S809 board discovered all the predicted defects — 53 DL-026, 8 DL-013, missing COSO citations, difficulty mismatches. (4) This required 4 subsequent sessions (S809.1, S810.1, S810, S811) to remediate what should have been caught pre-board. (5) Same pattern exists pool-wide: C-F (75 Unprocessed, 101 DL-013 fields), D-F (74 Unprocessed, 118 DL-013 fields), E-C (75 Unprocessed, DL-021 resolved but structurally unverified), C-E/D-E seeds all follow the Unprocessed→Board pattern with no pre-board scan. The pipeline treats 'Unprocessed' as 'ready for assessment' rather than 'needs structural scan first.'

gap_between_in_audit_and_actually_ready.description: The gap between 'In Audit' state and 'actually ready for certification board' is the entire pre-board structural defect scan. Items in 'Unprocessed' skip 'In Audit' entirely and proceed directly to the certification board. But even items that would enter 'In Audit' need 6 pre-board checks before being board-ready: DL-026 scan, DL-013 scan, DL-008 verification (with authoritative CC), COSO citation check, metadata completeness check (Difficulty↔Score, CL, AccountingPrinciple), and CC cross-verification (content-block vs metadata-block). None of these are automated or enforced. The S809 pipeline demonstrates that without these checks, items arrive at the board with 100% failure rate — not because they're bad items (Gate 1 passed, technical accuracy is sound), but because the content-authoring is incomplete and the gaps are structurally detectable.
gap_between_in_audit_and_actually_ready.estimated_gap_size: 6 structural scans + CC verification ≈ 3-5 minutes per item automated, or 1 agent session for a full section (≤75 items). The cost of NOT doing this: ~49 agent deployments across 4 sessions for 38 items (S809→S810 chain).
gap_between_in_audit_and_actually_ready.current_state_machine_bypass: QUESTION_METADATA_STANDARD.md §9.2 defines: Unprocessed → In Audit → Certified. S809 demonstrated the actual path: Unprocessed → Certification Board (skipping In Audit). The gap is the missing 'In Audit' pipeline — there is no automated structural scan that gates the Unprocessed→In Audit transition, so items arrive at the board with unknown defect load.

summary: The certification architecture has a systemic readiness gap: Unprocessed items reach certification boards without any pre-board structural defect scanning. The S809 Domain E seed pipeline demonstrates the full pathology. S808 seed inventory explicitly warned that 38 seeds needed structural defect scans (DL-008, DL-013, DL-026) before certification. No scans were run. The S809 certification board deployed 28 agents, assessed all 38 seeds, and found 100% blocked at Gate 2 (Explanation Quality) — 53 empty DL-026 slots, 8 DL-013 boilerplate slots, 97% missing COSO citations, 100% missing AccountingPrinciple fields, 60.5% difficulty overstated, 68.4% cognitive level misaligned. This triggered 4 follow-on sessions (S809.1, S810.1, S810, S811) — approximately 49 agent deployments — to remediate defects that were structurally detectable in under 5 minutes per item. The root causes are: (1) no automated pre-board scan pipeline exists, (2) DL-016 metadata-content CC shift corrupts the readiness scoring board's ability to correctly classify items, (3) the readiness board is advisory with no enforcement mechanism, (4) the Unprocessed→In Audit state machine transition is not enforced, (5) CorrectChoice is independently re-derived by each agent/board using different methodologies producing conflicting values. The readiness failure rate is 100% — zero items arriving at the S809 certification board were certifiable. The readiness board exists and correctly identifies blockers in some cases (S318) but cannot prevent certification boards from convening. Pre-board scan gaps total 11 distinct check types that were never run before items reached the board. This pattern is not limited to Domain E — sections C-F (101 DL-013 fields), D-F (118 DL-013 fields), E-C (75 unprocessed), and C-E/D-E seeds all follow the same Unprocessed→Board trajectory with zero pre-board structural verification.
recommendations: Implement automated Phase 0 pre-board structural scan gate (DL-026, DL-013, DL-008, COSO citation presence, EC quality thresholds, metadata completeness) — gate enforcement via governance-guard Rule 6.

Standardize CorrectChoice extraction: boundary-aware Function constructor same-object parse as sole authoritative method. Publish CC as Certified Pool Attribute — all agents reference CPA, don't independently re-derive.

Enforce Unprocessed→In Audit state transition: no item may reach certification board without passing automated structural scan. Add governance-guard rule blocking certification of any item not in 'In Audit' state.
Make readiness board verdict machine-enforceable: JSON boolean 'blocked' field prevents certification board from convening. Session startup protocol checks most recent readiness board verdict.
Run pre-board scans on ALL existing Unprocessed inventory (C-F, D-F, E-C, C-E seeds, D-E seeds) before they reach any certification board — approximately 342 items pool-wide.
Resolve DL-016 dual-block architecture before any further Pack C/D certification work — metadata-block vs. content-block CC divergence makes all certification assessments unreliable for these items.
